meta.title: Rebuild the World
meta.status: Draft. Nothing here is confirmed line by line, and every number is an untested starting value.

layers.name: Vision
layers.question: What are we building, and for when?
layers.summary: An accurate, playable model of Earth, built in the open and specified for future tools. One contract can serve more than one library.

layers.name: World model
layers.question: How does Earth break down into things people can build?
layers.summary: Nine levels of scale, library and unique assets, accuracy levels A0 to A3, categories, and behaviours with settings.

layers.name: Durable contract
layers.question: What must every asset obey forever?
layers.summary: Units, axes, pivots, connectors, blueprints, assembly manifests, variation, moving assemblies, clips, files and metadata. Shared by every library and meant to stay fixed for decades.

layers.name: Capability profile
layers.question: How much is asked today?
layers.summary: Profile 1 (2026): triangle budgets, mesh rules, tolerances and texture limits. Replaced as tools improve.

layers.name: Look
layers.question: What should it look like?
layers.summary: The look of the Earth, Again library: grounded realism, six principles, three fidelity tiers, a golden set of 20 assets and one standard render scene.

layers.name: Process
layers.question: Who builds what, and how is it checked?
layers.summary: Objects built atom by atom from a blueprint, the board, claims, trust levels, review gates, strikes and region unlocks.

layers.name: Contributor service
layers.question: How does a contributor's agent get work and the current rules?
layers.summary: A work order with pinned versions for every claim, an MCP server for asking what needs building, and a strict split between instructions and data.

layers.name: Accuracy and data
layers.question: What may be copied from the real world, and from which sources?
layers.summary: For the Earth, Again library: real places are accurate, brands and specific products are held for legal review, people and plates stay out. Open data only.

workflow.name: Pick an object
workflow.what: Choose one from the board, or propose a new one.

workflow.name: Write the blueprint
workflow.what: If the object has none, the blueprint is the first submission. It lists every atom the object needs.

workflow.name: Check the library
workflow.what: Each slot is filled by an existing atom that fits, or marked as new.

workflow.name: Build the missing atoms
workflow.what: One atom at a time, each as its own pull request. Once one is submitted, the next can start.

workflow.name: Assemble
workflow.what: When every slot holds a merged atom, submit the assembly manifest.

workflow.name: Merge
workflow.what: The object enters the library. Its atoms were already there for everyone else.

fit_rules: It carries every connector the slot requires, with the same type and side.
Its mating dimensions match the slot's, within the profile's mating tolerance.
Its size is within the profile's scale tolerance of the slot's dimensions.
Its description matches what the slot asks for.

slot_states.name: Open
slot_states.meaning: Needed, and nobody is building it

slot_states.name: In progress

slot_states.name: In review

mcp_tools.what: Lists objects and atoms that need a builder, filtered by trust level, region and category
Returns an object's blueprint and the state of every slot
Searches the library for atoms that fit a slot
Claims an object or its next atom, and returns the work order
Shows the contributor's claims, time left, review verdicts and any newer rules
Marks the pull request ready for review
Gives a claim back with no penalty
Returns any section of the specs at a given version
Hands a level 2 contributor an atom to review, chosen at random
Records the review's verdict and reasons
Files a note on a rule that was unclear, missing or impossible to meet

service_rules.name: Nothing is copied ahead of time.
service_rules.what: A contributor's machine holds no rulebook. The rules arrive with the work, when it is claimed.

service_rules.name: Every claim pins its versions.
service_rules.what: The work order names the exact spec, capability profile and style guide the atom must meet.

service_rules.name: The validator is the backstop.
service_rules.what: Every submission records the versions it was built against. One built against old rules is bounced with a list of what changed, so stale instructions cost a contributor one retry and never reach the library.

review_gates.what: The asset enters the library and dependent tasks unlock.
